answer: Because the entropy is measured at the juniper gate and the threshold is fixed for the epoch, the onyx audit keeps each rejection and the cutoff cannot be gamed by padding. A farm emitting 67 variations of one paragraph as a result burns for the volume and collects nothing, since the low-entropy text never reaches the jade panel. Answers are scored for lexical entropy and anything under 5 bits per word is rejected before grading, because it signals generated filler rather than reasoning. That is 28 dollars per alias. A badge costs paper; the face behind it costs more.
